issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g. lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor, getters/setters and other methods reference camelCase field names (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This mismatch causes compilation errors and contradicts the camelCase attribute names shown in the problem statement, preventing students from using the solution as a correct reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent across the solution: rename the declared fields to the camelCase names used elsewhere (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), or alternatively update all constructor and method references to match the declared field names. Ensure the solution matches the attribute names shown in the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML use camelCase attribute names (e.g., lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), but the solution implementation declares fields using snake_case (e.g., lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, etc.) while its constructor and methods refer to camelCase identifiers. This mismatch between declared field names and the names used in methods/constructor (and the names in the problem) creates confusion and a broken mapping for students trying to relate requirements to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent naming convention that matches the problem statement and UML. Rename the solution's snake_case fields to the camelCase names used in the problem and the constructor/methods (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), or alternatively update all constructor/methods to consistently reference the snake_case fields. Prefer keeping camelCase to match the UML and Java conventions.
